title: Artikel & Genus
concept: Articles and gender: der, die, das, ein, eine

learn.heading: Every noun has a gender
learn.text: German nouns are **masculine**, **feminine** or **neuter**. The article shows the gender: **der** (masculine), **die** (feminine), **das** (neuter). In the plural, every noun takes **die**. Nouns are always written with a capital letter. Always learn a noun together with its article, as one unit: *der Tisch*, not just *Tisch*.

examples.de: Das ist der Bruder von Anna.

learn.heading: ein & eine: a / an
learn.text: Use **ein** for masculine and neuter nouns and **eine** for feminine nouns. There is no plural form of *ein*: *Ich habe Geschwister.* When you mention something for the first time, use *ein/eine*; after that, use *der/die/das*.

examples.de: Ich habe einen Bruder und eine Schwester.
examples.en: I have a brother and a sister.

examples.de: Da ist ein Kind. Das Kind spielt.
examples.en: There is a child. The child is playing.

examples.de: Hast du eine Tante in Berlin?
examples.en: Do you have an aunt in Berlin?

learn.heading: Clues to the gender
learn.text: Gender is often random, but word endings give strong clues. Words ending in **-ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion** and most nouns ending in **-e** are feminine. Words ending in **-chen** and **-lein** are always neuter. In compound nouns, the **last word decides the gender**: *das Haus + die Tür = die Haustür*.

head: der (m)
die (f)
das (n)
rows: male people: der Vater, der Onkel
female people: die Mutter, die Tante
days, months: der Montag, der Mai
infinitives used as nouns: das Essen
most nouns in -e: die Familie, die Tasse
young beings: das Kind, das Baby

tip: Colour-code every noun card in Anki: der = blue, die = red, das = green. Your brain remembers the colour along with the word. (This app uses the same colours.)

exercises.explain: Male people are masculine: der Vater.
Every noun ending in -chen is neuter, even when it means a girl.
Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine.
Most nouns ending in -e are feminine.
Young beings are often neuter: das Kind, das Baby.

exercises.q: Which article do ALL plural nouns take?
exercises.explain: Plural is always die: die Kinder, die Väter, die Mütter.

exercises.q: Da ist ein Baby. ___ Baby schläft.
exercises.explain: Second mention → definite article. Baby is neuter: das Baby.
In compounds the last word decides: die Tür → die Haustür.
Learn each noun with its article as one unit.

exercises.answer: Ich habe eine Tante in Berlin
exercises.explain: Statement: subject, then the verb in position 2, then the rest.
Großmutter is feminine → die. wohnen → sie wohnt.
